unit: Unit 6: External Influences on Business Activity
scenario_stem:
Harrington Paper Works is a private limited company operating a paper and cardboard mill in the town of Kestrel Vale for 14 years, employing 240 workers. The mill generates $9,500,000 in annual revenue but its older boilers emit sulphur dioxide and the plant discharges wastewater. A government inspection found emissions 30% above the legal limit, exposing the company to daily fines of $8,000 until it complies.

Management is considering a $1,200,000 emissions control system, including new boilers and water treatment, to meet the legal limit. A local pressure group, Clean Air Kestrel, is campaigning against the mill and has urged two retail clients worth $2,000,000 a year to boycott its packaging. The company could instead continue operating and pay the fines while searching for cheaper equipment.

questions.question_text: Define 'pollution'.
questions.model_answer: The release of harmful substances, noise or energy into the environment in quantities that damage human health, wildlife or ecosystems [2].

knowledge_max_2: release of harmful substances, noise or energy into the environment
quantities that damage human health, wildlife or ecosystems

questions.question_text: Explain two problems pollution from the paper mill creates for Harrington Paper Works.
questions.model_answer: Problem 1: Heavy financial penalties [k], emissions 30% above the legal limit expose the mill to daily fines of $8,000 [app]. Problem 2: Reputational damage and lost orders [k], Clean Air Kestrel has urged two retail clients worth $2,000,000 a year to boycott its packaging [app].

knowledge_max_2: reputational damage / lost orders from boycott

questions.question_text: Explain two benefits to Harrington Paper Works of installing the $1,200,000 emissions control system.
questions.model_answer: Benefit 1: Stops the daily fines [k], the system brings the Kestrel Vale mill back within the legal limit so the $8,000 daily fines end [app], protecting profit [an]. Benefit 2: Protects customer orders [k], calming Clean Air Kestrel and defending the $2,000,000 of retail clients from the boycott [app], securing future sales [an].

questions.question_text: Do you think Harrington Paper Works should invest in the $1,200,000 emissions control system or continue paying the daily fines? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: Investing ends the fines permanently [k], bringing emissions 30% above the legal limit back within the law at Kestrel Vale so the $8,000 daily fines stop [app], saving up to $2,920,000 a year [an]. It also weakens the Clean Air Kestrel boycott threat and protects orders from retail clients worth $2,000,000 a year [app], securing future sales [an]. However, paying the fines avoids the immediate $1,200,000 outlay and preserves cash for 240 workers [k]. Overall, investing is the better option because the $2,920,000 annual saving far exceeds the one-off $1,200,000 cost within months [eval], and legal compliance also safeguards the mill's right to operate at Kestrel Vale long term [eval].

knowledge_max_2: ends the fines permanently / legal compliance
preserves short-term cash by paying fines
evaluation_max_2: weighs one-off $1,200,000 cost against recurring fine savings
compliance safeguards long-term right to operate

unit: Unit 6: External Influences on Business Activity
scenario_stem:
PalmCrest Estates is a private limited company operating 11,000 hectares of palm oil plantations in Country X, established 9 years ago by founder Renata Duarte. It employs 520 plantation workers and exports $6,800,000 of crude palm oil annually. To double output, the company plans to clear 1,500 hectares of remaining forest, expecting an extra $3,200,000 in annual sales.

Environmental groups claim the forest holds endangered primates and have organised a petition signed by 45,000 people. The government now requires an environmental impact assessment before any clearing, with fines of $500,000 for illegal logging. The board is weighing this against an alternative: buy 800 hectares of degraded, already-cleared land for $2,100,000, suited to replanting but with lower yields for the first 6 years of cultivation.

questions.question_text: Define 'deforestation'.
questions.model_answer: The clearing and permanent removal of trees and forest cover from land, usually to make way for farming, logging or development [2].

knowledge_max_2: clearing and permanent removal of trees and forest cover
to make way for farming, logging or development

questions.question_text: Explain two problems that clearing 1,500 hectares of forest could cause for PalmCrest Estates.
questions.model_answer: Problem 1: Legal penalties [k], the government now requires an environmental impact assessment and illegal logging brings fines of $500,000 [app]. Problem 2: Reputational damage and lost sales [k], the petition signed by 45,000 people shows strong opposition to clearing the forest [app].

questions.question_text: Explain two advantages for PalmCrest Estates of buying the 800 hectares of degraded land instead of clearing the forest.
questions.model_answer: Advantage 1: No legal risk [k], already-cleared degraded land avoids the environmental impact assessment problem and the $500,000 illegal logging fine [app], removing the risk of losing the expansion programme [an]. Advantage 2: Protects reputation and exports [k], replanting degraded land keeps the $6,800,000 export business safe from the 45,000-signature petition [app], supporting continued sales growth [an].

analysis_max_2: removing the risk of losing the expansion programme

questions.question_text: Do you think PalmCrest Estates should buy the degraded land instead of clearing the 1,500 hectares of forest? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: Buying the degraded land avoids fines and rejection [k], because the government requires an environmental impact assessment and illegal logging brings fines of $500,000 [app], protecting the company's legal position and expansion plan [an]. It also safeguards the $6,800,000 export business, since buyers increasingly prefer sustainable palm oil while 45,000 people have signed the petition [app], securing long-term contracts [an]. However, clearing the forest could unlock $3,200,000 in extra sales quickly [k], boosting growth for 520 workers. Overall, buying the degraded land is wiser because the $2,100,000 price is outweighed by avoiding the $500,000 fine risk and reputational harm [eval], and sustainable replanting keeps the estates compliant and attractive to export buyers for years to come [eval].

knowledge_max_2: avoids fines and rejection / legal compliance
clearing forest unlocks extra sales quickly
analysis_max_2: protecting the company's legal position and expansion plan
evaluation_max_2: weighs $2,100,000 purchase price against $500,000 fine and reputational harm
sustainable replanting keeps estates compliant and attractive to buyers

unit: Unit 6: External Influences on Business Activity
scenario_stem:
BrightKiln Cement Works is a private limited company running a cement plant on the edge of the town of Alderney for 18 years, employing 150 workers and producing 90,000 tonnes of cement a year, with $11,000,000 in annual revenue. Local residents complain about night-time grinding noise of around 60 decibels, dust and lorry traffic passing up to 200 homes.

A residents' association has collected 1,200 signatures demanding action. A planned $750,000 noise barrier and enclosed conveyor would cut noise by 25 decibels, but shareholders want a $1,400,000 plant expansion next year that would double output. The local council has warned that continued breaches could bring an enforcement notice and possible closure. Alternatively, management could move night shifts to daytime, cutting capacity by 20%.

questions.question_text: Define 'noise pollution'.
questions.model_answer: Unwanted or excessive sound that harms the health and quality of life of people living or working near its source, such as machinery or lorry traffic [2].

knowledge_max_2: harms the health and quality of life of people nearby

questions.question_text: Explain two external costs the BrightKiln Cement Works plant creates for the local community.
questions.model_answer: External cost 1: Noise disturbing homes [k], night-time grinding of around 60 decibels disturbs residents near the Alderney plant [app]. External cost 2: Dust and traffic pollution [k], lorries passing up to 200 homes and dust from the plant have driven 1,200 residents to sign the association's petition [app].

questions.question_text: Explain two benefits to BrightKiln Cement Works of installing the $750,000 noise barrier and enclosed conveyor.
questions.model_answer: Benefit 1: Avoids closure [k], cutting noise by 25 decibels answers the council's warning over the 60 decibels night-time breaches [app], protecting $11,000,000 of annual revenue and 150 jobs [an]. Benefit 2: Repairs community relations [k], easing the complaints of the 1,200-signature residents' association [app], strengthening the plant's licence to operate and planning position [an].

analysis_max_2: protecting $11,000,000 of annual revenue and 150 jobs
strengthening the plant's licence to operate and planning position

questions.question_text: Do you think BrightKiln Cement Works should install the $750,000 noise barrier and enclosed conveyor or move night shifts to daytime? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: The barrier permanently cuts noise by 25 decibels [k], removing the 60 decibels night-time breach that risks the council's enforcement notice and closure [app], safeguarding $11,000,000 annual revenue and 150 jobs [an]. It also defuses the 1,200-signature residents' petition, easing future planning consents [app], which supports the planned $1,400,000 expansion [an]. However, moving night shifts to daytime avoids the $750,000 cost entirely [k], preserving short-term cash, though cutting capacity by 20% reduces sales. Overall, installing the barrier is the stronger option because avoiding closure and the 20% capacity loss outweighs the one-off $750,000 [eval], and permanent noise control protects the $1,400,000 expansion and community support the plant needs [eval].

knowledge_max_2: barrier permanently resolves the noise breach
moving night shifts avoids the cost / preserves short-term cash
evaluation_max_2: weighs closure risk and 20% capacity loss against one-off $750,000
permanent noise control protects expansion and community support

unit: Unit 6: External Influences on Business Activity
scenario_stem:
Eastmere Brickworks is a private limited company planning to build a new brick factory in the deprived town of Darnley Moor, creating 180 permanent jobs and a training academy expected to train 120 young people a year. Construction will cost $5,500,000 and take 18 months. The local council supports the scheme and has offered a 4-year business rates holiday worth $600,000.

The site sits beside 40 homes, and residents worry about lorry movements of up to 90 trucks a day, plus smoke from the kiln. The company could instead build on out-of-town land 12 kilometres away, avoiding complaints but adding $1,100,000 in transport costs and losing the rates holiday. Local unemployment in Darnley Moor is 9%, well above the national average.

questions.question_text: Define 'external benefits'.
questions.model_answer: Benefits enjoyed by third parties who are not directly involved in a business decision, such as jobs, training or regeneration in the local community [2].

knowledge_max_2: not directly involved in the decision, e.g. jobs, training, regeneration

questions.question_text: Explain two external benefits the Eastmere Brickworks factory would create in Darnley Moor.
questions.model_answer: External benefit 1: New jobs [k], 180 permanent jobs in a town where unemployment is 9% [app]. External benefit 2: Training and skills [k], the training academy is expected to train 120 young people a year [app].

questions.question_text: Explain two advantages for Eastmere Brickworks of building on out-of-town land instead of in Darnley Moor.
questions.model_answer: Advantage 1: Fewer complaints and delays [k], the out-of-town site avoids 90 trucks a day passing 40 homes [app], reducing the risk of objections [an]. Advantage 2: Lower environmental friction [k], no kiln smoke issues for neighbours eases pressure on planning and operations [app], protecting the 18-month construction timetable [an].

questions.question_text: Do you think Eastmere Brickworks should build the factory in Darnley Moor or on out-of-town land 12 kilometres away? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: The town site creates strong community support [k], bringing 180 jobs and training academy places for 120 young people a year to Darnley Moor where unemployment is 9% [app], while saving $1,100,000 in transport costs plus the $600,000 rates holiday [an]. However, the out-of-town site avoids 90 trucks a day passing 40 homes and kiln smoke complaints [app], reducing the risk of objections [k] and protecting the 18-month construction timetable [an]. Overall, the town site is the better option because the combined $1,700,000 saving outweighs the local complaint risk [eval], and regenerating a high-unemployment community strengthens the brickworks' reputation and future planning applications [eval].

knowledge_max_2: community support and regeneration from town site
out-of-town site avoids complaints and objection risk
analysis_max_2: saving $1,100,000 in transport plus the $600,000 holiday boosts profit
evaluation_max_2: weighs the $1,700,000 combined saving against local complaint risk
regeneration strengthens reputation and future planning applications

unit: Unit 6: External Influences on Business Activity
scenario_stem:
Velvette Apparel is a private limited company designing fashion clothing sold through 25 stores, founded 7 years ago by Priya Raman, generating $18,000,000 in annual revenue. Its cheapest supplier in Country Y produces garments for $4 per unit compared with $9 from a certified ethical supplier, saving Velvette $1,250,000 a year at current volumes. An audit found the Country Y factory pays below the legal minimum wage and enforces excessive overtime.

The board must choose between renewing the Country Y contract for 3 years, switching fully to the ethical supplier and raising prices by 8%, or splitting orders 50/50. A survey showed 62% of 3,000 customers would pay more for ethically made clothes. The Country Y contract supports 900 factory workers in Country Y, who would lose their jobs if Velvette switched overnight.

questions.question_text: Identify two ethical issues businesses may face when choosing suppliers.
questions.model_answer: Low pay and below the legal minimum wage for supplier workers [1]; excessive overtime and poor working conditions at supplier factories [1].

questions.question_text: Explain two reasons why the Country Y contract creates an ethical problem for Velvette Apparel.
questions.model_answer: Reason 1: Exploitation of workers [k], the audit found the Country Y factory pays below the legal minimum wage for the $4 garments it supplies [app]. Reason 2: Unfair working conditions [k], enforcing excessive overtime at the factory producing Velvette's clothing [app].

knowledge_max_2: exploitation of workers / below minimum wage

questions.question_text: Explain two benefits to Velvette Apparel of switching fully to the certified ethical supplier.
questions.model_answer: Benefit 1: Higher customer loyalty and sales [k], 62% of 3,000 customers would pay more for ethically made clothes [app], lifting revenue beyond the 8% price rise [an]. Benefit 2: Better reputation and lower risk [k], avoiding future scandals like the Country Y audit findings [app], protecting the $18,000,000 brand [an].

analysis_max_2: lifting revenue beyond the 8% price rise

questions.question_text: Do you think Velvette Apparel should switch completely to the certified ethical supplier or keep the Country Y contract? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: Switching completely protects Velvette from exploitation scandals [k], ending reliance on the below minimum wage Country Y factory supplying $4 garments [app], defending the $18,000,000 brand and 25 stores [an]. With 62% of 3,000 surveyed customers willing to pay more, the 8% price rise could hold sales [app], supporting profit despite higher unit costs [an]. However, keeping the Country Y contract saves $1,250,000 a year, avoids job losses for 900 workers and spares the 8% price rise [k]. Overall, switching is the better option because ethical sourcing matches the 62% customer preference and removes audit risk [eval], even though it trims short-term margin, as brand trust outlasts $1,250,000 of annual savings [eval].

knowledge_max_2: keeping the contract saves money and jobs
application_max_2: below minimum wage Country Y factory / $4 garments
analysis_max_2: the 8% price rise could hold sales despite higher costs
evaluation_max_2: weighs 62% customer preference and audit risk against $1,250,000 savings

unit: Unit 6: External Influences on Business Activity
scenario_stem:
Brookfield Supermarkets is a regional chain of 14 stores in Country X operating for 11 years, with 1,050 staff and $26,000,000 in annual sales. Electricity costs rose 28% last year, and refrigeration alone now costs $780,000 a year. Management is considering replacing open fridge units with doors and LED lighting across all stores for $2,300,000, saving an estimated $410,000 a year.

A loyalty survey of 9,000 customers found 58% prefer to shop with energy-efficient retailers, and a competitor chain recently launched an advertising campaign highlighting its green energy use. Brookfield could instead phase the change over 3 years to spread the cost, delaying most of the savings. Two banks have offered loans at 7.5% interest to fund the project immediately.

questions.question_text: Define 'green consumer'.
questions.model_answer: A customer who deliberately chooses products and services that cause less environmental damage, sometimes willing to pay a premium for them [2].

questions.question_text: Explain two reasons why Brookfield Supermarkets might want to reduce its energy use.
questions.model_answer: Reason 1: Lower operating costs [k], electricity costs rose 28% last year and refrigeration alone now costs $780,000 a year [app]. Reason 2: Attract green-minded customers [k], a loyalty survey of 9,000 customers showed 58% prefer energy-efficient retailers [app].

questions.question_text: Explain two advantages to Brookfield Supermarkets of installing fridge doors and LED lighting now.
questions.model_answer: Advantage 1: Immediate energy savings [k], the $2,300,000 upgrade saves an estimated $410,000 a year across 14 stores [app], raising profit [an]. Advantage 2: Competitive advantage [k], acting now answers the 58% customer preference and the competitor's green energy campaign [app], strengthening customer loyalty and sales [an].

questions.question_text: Do you think Brookfield Supermarkets should install the fridge doors and LED lighting now, or phase the change over 3 years? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: Installing now captures savings immediately [k], delivering the estimated $410,000 a year across 14 stores from a $2,300,000 investment [app], recovering the cost in under 6 years and raising profit [an]. It also positions Brookfield ahead of the competitor's green campaign, matching the 58% of 9,000 surveyed shoppers who prefer energy-efficient retailers [app], building loyalty and repeat sales [an]. However, phasing over 3 years spreads the $2,300,000 and avoids a 7.5% loan [k], easing pressure on cash flow. Overall, installing now is the better option because delaying forfeits a large share of the $410,000 annual saving [eval], and the 28% electricity rise makes early action cheaper than waiting [eval].

knowledge_max_2: phasing spreads the cost and eases cash flow
analysis_max_2: recovering the cost in under 6 years and raising profit
evaluation_max_2: weighs delay against forfeited savings

unit: Unit 6: External Influences on Business Activity

Suncrest Soft Drinks is a private limited company producing bottled fruit juices and sodas, founded 12 years ago by Daniel and Ruth Okoro, with $13,000,000 in annual sales through 2,400 retail outlets. Posting the honest campaign on social media costs nothing extra, and the founders must approve by Friday.

unit: Unit 6: External Influences on Business Activity
